text:
sara_sales: Hey team — FinCorp just kicked off an on‑prem POC. key constraints: fully air‑walled site (no outbound), strict upgrade windows (monthly patch window only), and limited bandwidth for image transfers. They're asking about packaging options, expected bundle sizes for delta updates, upgrade cadence we can support, and how pricing would look for a short‑term POC vs reserved capacity. Can @nate_se or @ben_arch weigh in on feasibility?

nate_se: Short answer: doable but a few tradeoffs. Need to confirm two things from FinCorp: 1) whether they accept signed delta bundles delivered via USB/airgap transfer, and 2) max single‑file size they can receive.

sara_sales: They said max per transfer ~200 MB, and USB workflow is allowed.

ben_arch: Good — that clarifies a lot. Our recommended approach: produce a compact "minibundle" for day‑0 bootstrap (~150–300 MB depending on model quantization) and ship subsequent patches as signed delta chunks. Full model images (non‑quantized) can be several GB; we avoid shipping full unless absolutely necessary.

ben_arch: Suggested cadence we normally offer for air‑gapped customers:
- POC phase: 1 initial bootstrap bundle + weekly small deltas during evaluation (only if they opt in)
- Production: monthly security/critical patches + quarterly minor improvements + yearly major upgrades (opt‑in)
This meshes with limited bandwidth and predictable ops windows.

nate_se: For the delta strategy we use binary diffs + metadata: typical delta chunk size = 20–50 MB (depends on quantization and model layer changes). For example, between two quantized checkpoints a daily delta can be ~30 MB.

laura_sec: Security questions — we need to ensure: SBOM attached to every bundle, signed with our HSM/KMS, and verification code in the on‑prem agent. We can provide the signing public key for them to pin and verify offline. Also require CVE scan report for any third‑party libs included.

laura_sec: For compliance checklist:
- Bundle signature (RSA/ECDSA) :thumbsup:
- SBOM (CycloneDX) included
- Reproducible build hashes
- Signed release notes
We have a template security questionnaire (I'll drop link).

ops-bot: Deployment artifact ready check: bootstrap_bundle_v1.tar.gz (sha256: 9f3b...) size 182 MB — signed. CI: artifact-signer/2026-03-18 -> success ✅

nate_se: Example agent config snippet we recommend to enforce signature verification (they can paste into their operator manifest):
```yaml
agent: 
  update: 
    mode: airgap
    signature_check: true
    allowed_sources: ["usb", "local-sftp"]
    max_chunk_mb: 200
```

sara_sales: Great. On pricing — FinCorp asked about POC discounts and conversion to reserved capacity. Any quick numbers?

nate_se: POC pricing is flat for 30 days: $6k for a single reserved node equivalent used in POC (includes support during the window). If they convert to a 12‑month reserved commit within 60 days of the POC completion we can credit 50% of the POC fee toward the first invoice. For air‑gapped add‑ons (signed bundles, extended retention for audit logs, on‑site support day) we price a one‑time packaging fee — typically $2,500–8,000 depending on automation level.

ben_arch: Note on operational blockers: if they require zero human touch (we cannot provide any connectivity at all), then upgrades must be fully scripted client‑side. That increases automation work (we charge the packaging fee above). If they allow scheduled controlled egress for checksums only (1‑way pull telemetry), we can reduce the packaging fee.

laura_sec: I'll start the security questionnaire and send the template. Also need to flag: their legal asked about FIPS crypto for signing — we support HSM signing workflows but need to validate their KMS/HSM model.

sara_sales: Thanks all. I'll collect FinCorp answers on max file size and whether temporary outbound for checksums is acceptable. Can we have a quick sync tomorrow if they confirm? :calendar:

nate_se: Yes — I'm free 10–11am PT. I'll prepare an estimate of delta sizes and a sample minibundle.

ben_arch: I'll prepare a short ops runbook for USB transfer and rollback steps (2–3 pages).

laura_sec: I'll prefill the security template with our defaults so they can see gaps quickly.

sara_sales: Perfect. attaching the customer's short questionnaire answers so far: <link to doc>. Follow ups tomorrow. Thanks! :rocket:
